answer: Each new identity must join an eight-member mutual-insurance pool. Each locks 60 credits in a vault and signs a pearl note for each poolmate; the pool ledger and delta register publish all bonds and slashes for public recomputation. If one member is proved sybil, the pool's 480 credits are slashed, so members vet hard before signing. Fakes cannot stack in one pool: the kth fake needs its own 60-credit bond in a fresh pool, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits. Renting notes fails: a reused pearl signature on two pools voids both and slashes the signer. An honest newcomer pays only one bond.
